title: A Homecoming for the Group Chat
premise: Lena Dunmore has spent seven years being the responsible one — cooking, cleaning, and raising her younger siblings while her mother works hospital night shifts. When the ghost haunting Hollow Creek High begins leaving her handwritten notes in ink that vanishes by morning, she learns the spirit is the school's most famous dropout, a girl who died in 1968 after sacrificing everything for her own family and never got to live. As the notes push Lena toward prom, first love, and a scholarship she's too scared to claim, Lena uncovers what the ghost actually wants: not vengeance, but a witness. On prom night, Lena must choose between repeating the ghost's fate of quiet self-erasure or breaking the cycle — and helping the spirit finally go home.
about_author: Tamsin Lockridge is a former night-shift nurse who writes young adult fiction about kids who grow up too fast. She lives in a drafty farmhouse with three cats and an unhealthy attachment to group chats.

chapters.title: The Careful Girl
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A chaotic morning establishes the Dunmore household: Lena managing siblings Milo and Junie, mom's exhaustion, and Lena's own invisible role at school. She declines a party invitation without hesitation. Emotional beat: the quiet ache of competence — she's good at this life, and it's suffocating her.

chapters.title: Ink That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the library's back stacks, Lena finds a note reading 'You look tired, Lena Dunmore' in shimmering violet ink that fades before her eyes. No one claims it; security footage shows nothing. Emotional beat: unease curdling into a thrilling, terrifying sense of being seen for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Group Chat Ghost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Lena and best friend Priya. The notes become a school-wide phenomenon, but only Lena's are personal. Priya starts a conspiracy group chat that accidentally goes viral. Emotional beat: comedic relief masking Lena's growing dread that the ghost knows things about her no living person does.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Left Behind
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Researching yearbooks, Lena identifies the ghost: Marguerite Hale, class of 1968, who vanished senior year and died young. The notes begin asking questions: 'Who cooks dinner tonight? Who dreams?' Emotional beat: recognition — Lena sees her own life reflected in a girl fifty years dead.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Noticed
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Lena and Theo Vasquez, the scholarship student who's been leaving anonymous snacks in her locker since freshman year. He asks her to prom; she says no out of duty. That night, a note appears: 'Marguerite said no once. Ask her how it ended.' Emotional beat: longing versus guilt.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: Mom's POV. A missed promotion and a health scare force Mom to confront how much she's outsourced to her eldest daughter. A raw kitchen-table fight erupts when she finds Lena's hidden scholarship application, unsigned. Emotional beat: love expressed as burden, both women drowning in duty they chose for each other.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The ghost leads Lena through a vision of Marguerite's final months: giving up college, a forbidden love, and dying unremarked while her family thrived on her sacrifice. Lena realizes the notes aren't haunting — they're warning. Emotional beat: grief and fury fusing into resolve.

chapters.title: Prom Is a Trap (Or a Door)
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Prom approaches; the whole school is watching the 'ghost girl.' Milo gets sick, Junie panics, and every obligation conspires to keep Lena home. Theo shows up at her door anyway. Emotional beat: the walls closing in, and one stubborn hand reaching through them.

chapters.title: The Night of the Vanishing Ink
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At prom, Marguerite manifests fully and offers Lena a bargain: take her place as the careful ghost, and be free of duty forever — or refuse and carry the weight alone. Lena refuses both, declaring that survival shouldn't cost your whole self, and speaks Marguerite's name aloud so someone finally remembers her. Emotional beat: climax — choosing neither martyrdom nor escape, but wholeness.

chapters.title: A Homecoming
chapters.summary: Epilogue-style, shifting among all four Dunmore siblings' POVs. Marguerite's ink fades for good, leaving one last note: 'Go live loudly.' Mom renegotiates the household load; Lena signs the scholarship; she and Theo slow-dance in the kitchen instead of a gym. Emotional beat: resolution — inheritance redefined as love passed forward, not sacrifice passed down.
